To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the magnetic signal of submarine basaltic rocks is controlled by the oxidation state of the titanomagnetite; (2) the oxidation of titanomagnetite is a function of the time that has elapsed since emplacement of the basalt; (3) the oxidation state of submarine basalts is a function of depth in the oceanic crust; and (4) the magnetic signal from a given depth in the crust is a function of age.
the oceanic crust is strongly oxidized by the time it is about 16 Ma old, and that the magnetic signal is strongly viscous.
the magnetic properties of submarine basalt are controlled primarily by oxidation state and that the magnetic properties change with time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin and evolution of the magnetic field of the Earth.
the nature of magnetic minerals in submarine basalts and with the origin of magnetic anomalies in the oceanic crust.
the magnetic properties of submarine basaltic rocks recovered from Leg 37 of DSDP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic signal of a rock is the sum of the magnetic signals of its individual minerals.

1) the magnetic properties of basalts from the Mid-Atlantic ridge are consistent with the hypothesis that the rocks were oxidized during their cooling history; 2) the degree of oxidation is greater for the older rocks; 3) the magnetic properties are consistent with the presence of a high-Curietemperature phase, magnetite; and 4) the magnetic properties do not provide evidence for a significant change in the oxidation state of the basalts during their cooling history.

the magnetic properties of the basalts studied here are consistent with the hypothesis that the magnetic signal of submarine basalts is a function of age, and that the signal is a function of the degree of oxidation of titanomagnetite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic mineralogy of the basalts is dominated by titanomagnetite and is strongly affected by the oxidation state of the rocks.
the magnetic properties of the basalts recovered from the ocean floor at 37°N are consistent with a model of progressive oxidation of the titanomagnetite grains in the basalts with increasing age.

the magnetic properties of the oceanic basalts are strongly affected by the oxidation of titanomagnetite and that the oxidation is related to the age of the basalts and to the water depth of the oceanic basement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic signature of the crust can be very different from the magnetic signature of a single rock sample.
the oceanic crust is a much more dynamic system than we previously thought.
the magnetization of the oceanic lithosphere is controlled by its magnetic properties, which are in turn controlled by oxidation state.
